prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1102; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Records show long-standing treatment for the same condition before the crash; most of the current complaints come from it.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Nobody gave the claimant's name at the scene; the claimant joined the claim days later.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by phone to the adjuster line. The caller describes being struck while turning left at an intersection and reports a concussion, with symptoms beginning shortly after the impact.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy file. The driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy, and the coverage period in effect covers the reported loss.

Entry 3: The claimant has no legal representation at this time and is handling the claim directly. Explained the documentation needed for the injury and vehicle portions.

Entry 4: Photos of the vehicle were received from the claimant. They confirm several of the described details, though the images do not show the full sequence of the collision.

Entry 5: Inspected the damaged areas. Most of the damage is in line with the impact described, and the force shown on the front and side panels fits the reported crash.

Entry 6: A few older scratches were noted on the rear bumper. They may predate this incident and will be set aside for the repair estimate.

Entry 7: Checked for independent witnesses. None were identified at the scene, and the police report does not list any.

Entry 8: Spoke with the claimant again. The account of how the collision occurred matches what was given in the first call, including the turning movement and the point of impact.

Entry 9: Medical records were requested. The initial treatment for the head injury fits the kind and force of the crash, and the course of care was typical, with symptoms easing as the claimant improved.

Entry 10: Records also show treatment for the same condition well before this crash. Much of the current complaint appears to stem from that earlier history, so this is being weighed carefully.

Entry 11: The claimant was not identified at the scene and first contacted the carrier several days after the collision. The delay and the earlier records are noted in the file for review.

Entry 12: Nothing so far suggests the vehicle damage occurred before the coverage start date. Next steps are the repair estimate, the full medical review, and a decision on the bodily injury portion once the records are complete.
